content.user_title: Add Backend HTTP Outcalls to Motoko Canisters
content.value_statement: Backend canisters often need external API data without routing through frontend code. This skill shows how to add Caffeine AI HTTP outcall helpers for GET and POST requests.
actual_capabilities: Describes the caffeineai-http-outcalls module for backend Motoko canisters.
Shows the transform callback pattern required for Internet Computer HTTP outcalls.
Provides a backend GET request example using OutCall.httpGetRequest.
Identifies POST request support through the same helper module.
Notes that JSON parsing should be handled outside Motoko when needed.
limitations: Does not include a complete POST implementation example.
Does not provide URL allow-listing or response validation logic.
Does not parse JSON responses inside Motoko.
Assumes a Caffeine AI Motoko backend canister project.

use_cases.description: Add a Motoko GET outcall for data that should be fetched by the backend canister.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Backend Outcalls
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how this skill helps a Caffeine AI Motoko backend canister make HTTP outcalls. Keep the explanation practical.

prompt_templates.title: Add a GET Outcall
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a backend HTTP GET outcall to my Motoko canister using the caffeineai-http-outcalls helper module.

prompt_templates.title: Plan POST Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the steps for adding a backend HTTP POST outcall with safe headers and clear response handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Outcall Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my backend outcall design for URL validation, credential handling, transform callbacks, and frontend JSON parsing boundaries.

output_examples.input: Add a backend GET outcall for a weather API.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines the module import, transform callback, request helper, and where to pass the approved API URL.

output_examples.input: Review my plan for POST requests from the canister.
output: Checks whether the outbound host is approved.
Flags any credentials placed in visible source or prompts.
Recommends frontend parsing for JSON-heavy responses.

output_examples.input: Explain why the frontend should not perform this outcall.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains backend ownership of the outcall and separates canister logic from frontend response presentation.

best_practices: Validate and allow-list external URLs before backend canisters call them.
Keep API credentials out of prompts, examples, and visible source files.
Use the transform callback consistently for Internet Computer HTTP outcall responses.
anti_patterns: Passing arbitrary user-entered URLs directly to backend outcall helpers.
Embedding API keys in Motoko examples or prompt text.
Expecting frontend code to replace backend HTTP outcall logic.

faq.question: Does this skill run HTTP requests itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides implementation of backend canister HTTP outcalls using a Caffeine AI helper module.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover both GET and POST requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents helper functions for GET and POST, with a complete GET usage example.

faq.question: Can it parse JSON in Motoko?
faq.answer: No. The skill notes that JSON parsing is not directly supported in Motoko.

faq.question: Is this only for Caffeine AI projects?
faq.answer: It is written for Caffeine AI Motoko projects that use the caffeineai-http-outcalls dependency.

faq.question: What security checks should users add?
faq.answer: Users should validate target URLs, protect credentials, review headers, and control response handling.
